title: `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler and a 267 MB dev tree into all 24 runtime images — KS-490 closed the service tree only
description:
## KS-490 closed the SERVICE tree and left the SHARED tree open — `/shared` ships the TypeScript compiler into all 24 runtime images

KS-490's two PRs (#849, #851) removed the build toolchain from the runtime *stages* and pruned each service's *own* `node_modules`. **Neither touches** `/shared`, and every runtime stage copies it wholesale.

### Measured on the live demo box, in RUNNING containers

| Reading | `secuura-security` | `secuura-governance` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/shared/node_modules/typescript` | **present, 22.9 MB** | **present, 22.9 MB** |
| `bin/tsc` | **present** | **present** |
| `/shared` total | **267.2 MB** | **267.2 MB** |
| top-level entries under `/shared/node_modules` | **243** | **243** |

*(The #851 gate's tester reported 342 packages; I counted **243 top-level entries** with* `ls | wc -l`*, which counts a scoped* `@org` *directory once regardless of what it contains. Both numbers are probably right about different things — stating my instrument rather than reconciling them by assertion.)*

### It is footprint and attack surface, NOT loadability — measured, with a control

```
require.resolve('typescript', {paths:['/app']})  ->  MODULE_NOT_FOUND
require.resolve('express',    {paths:['/app']})  ->  resolves
```

The control is what makes the first line meaningful: the resolver works, and `typescript` genuinely is not reachable from the app's module paths. So no runtime code can load it — but a compiler binary and 267 MB of dev tree are present in every running container, which is exactly what KS-490 exists to remove.

### Cause

`shared-builder` runs `npm ci` **without** `--omit=dev` and is never pruned, and all 24 runtime stages `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared`.

### Fix shape — and the hazard it carries

Prune `shared-builder` after its build: one place, all 24 services.

⚠ **This is exactly the hazard #851 just fixed.** `@secuura/shared` is a hand-made undeclared symlink; pruning removed it, and three runtime stages that did not re-create it shipped images that crashed on start with `Cannot find module '@secuura/shared'`. **A** `/shared` **prune therefore needs a real start probe per service, not reasoning** — the same shape of evidence #851 ended up needing. See [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) and #851's fix commit.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #851's gate findings (F1).*

nodes.body:
## The 342-vs-243 count, settled — and 342 is not reproduced by any instrument I ran

Wednesday's instruction was to settle this with **one named instrument and say which**, not to reconcile it by assertion. Here is what each candidate instrument actually returns.

### 243 is settled, and two independent instruments agree exactly

| instrument | environment | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| distinct top-level directory names in `packages/shared/package-lock.json` (a scoped `@x/y` contributes the directory `@x` once) | the repo alone, no container | **243** |
| `ls /shared/node_modules \| wc -l` | running container `secuura-security`, local stack | **243** |

The lockfile is the artefact that *decides* what lands in `/shared`, and it needs no container — anyone can reproduce it from the repo. It agrees with the container to the unit. **s140's 243 is correct and is a directory count.**

Control on that instrument: `ls -A` returns **245**; the two extra are `.bin` and `.package-lock.json`, which `ls` omits. So the pair can differ, and does.

### The other number — what each plausible instrument gives

| instrument | result |
| -- | -- |
| top-level **packages** in the lockfile (scoped counted individually) | 306 |
| every package entry in the lockfile (top-level + nested) | 347 |
| installed top-level package dirs, in the container | 301 |
| **all installed package dirs** (top-level + scoped + nested), in the container | **324** |
| `find /shared/node_modules -name package.json` | 722 |
| the same, capped at depth 3 | 483 |

**None of them is 342.** The nearest are 324 and 347.

Two things that fall out of this and are worth keeping:

- **`find -name package.json` is not a package-count instrument.** It returns 722 and 483 depending only on the depth cap, because packages ship their own sub-manifests (`dist/package.json`, `esm/package.json`). This was the instrument I had *predicted* I would use; it would have produced a confident wrong number. Measured before trusting.
- **The lockfile and the container legitimately differ**: 306 top-level in the lock against 301 installed, and 41 nested against 23. That is the expected shape for optional/platform-specific packages that do not install on this architecture — the lock describes every platform, the container holds one.

### So: 342 is UNREPRODUCED, not reconciled

I am not going to invent a derivation that lands on 342. The honest state is that the tester's figure does not match any instrument I ran, and the two candidates it could plausibly be (324 all-installed-dirs, 347 all-lock-entries) are 18 and 5 away. **If the tester names their instrument, it can be settled in one command; until then this is an open discrepancy, not a resolved one.**

What it does **not** change: 243 directories is right, and the finding this ticket exists for is unaffected by which package-count instrument is used.

### The footprint finding itself — re-measured, and it stands

Measured in the running container `secuura-security` on the **local** stack (stated explicitly; s140's identical figures came from the **demo** box, so the two environments agree):

```
/shared                                    267.2 MB
/shared/node_modules/typescript            present
/shared/node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc    present
```

Same total to the tenth of a megabyte as s140's demo reading, which is a useful corroboration across two environments.

**Nothing was changed.** Read-only `docker exec`, local stack. The demo box was not touched and stays pinned at `db1848abf`.

### Still to do on this ticket
The prune itself, which carries the hazard the ticket already names — the same one #851 paid for — so it needs **a start probe per service, not reasoning**. That is the next piece of work and it is not started. [KS-921](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-921)'s guard (PR #870) is the structural protection against exactly the failure a `/shared` prune would risk, so the two are worth landing in that order.

*Measured by s141 (seat A), 2026-09-06.*
